walkthrough: Min 0-3: WhatsApp link opens on phone. It asks 'What's the problem?' like texting. I type 'sales down 20% this quarter' with my thumbs. It feels natural, like talking to my staff.
Min 3-10: One question at a time (which channel, which product, when it started). Easy in a 15-min burst. I stop when the kettle boils or a staff member calls. The chat is saved, so I resume.
Min 10: Engagement page is created and the chat moves to a side panel. On a phone a side panel is probably a drawer or a separate screen, and I may not understand where the chat went. Stuck point 1.

Day 1 evening: 'Your next step' card says 'Connect Shopify, 2 min'. I tap it and OAuth works. For the WhatsApp export, the sales team owns it, so I tap invite and send it to the sales manager. Odoo export: I hate exports, so I tap 'we don't have it' and see what happens instead. Total about 12 min.

Day 2 reframe: the consultant has confirmed its understanding. I realise stock is the real issue. I open the side panel and type 'Actually the problem is that our best-selling line will run out of stock for months. How do we grow without it?'. It's the same texting I've already been doing, so I don't need to find an edit button. The risk is whether the page's 'What we understood' and the data checklist update, or whether it asks me to confirm first. Stuck point 2: I'm not sure the old sales-drop work is dropped, because the answer 'can turn into page changes'. I also need to give it stock and supplier lead-time data that wasn't on the list. About 6 min.

Day 3-4: Waiting states are clear ('we're working, expected Thu'). WhatsApp ping with a link to the action. I read the report on my phone, then export to PDF to forward to my ops head. Long finding tables on a small screen are heavy but the one-paragraph answer on top is enough.
Abandon risk: low. The only likely drop-off is the first phone moment of the chat-to-page switch, or if the reframe makes me redo the data list.
Z.quote: I just told it 'actually the problem is stock' the way I'd tell my manager, and the page changed. That is how I want to work. I only worry about the side panel on a small screen.

walkthrough: Min 0-3: Open the link on my phone. One chat. 'What's the problem you want solved?' I type it. This is the same as WhatsApp and needs no learning.
Min 3-10: One question at a time. Fine. The 'what we understood' summary arrives as a message and I tap confirm.

Day 1: Data items arrive as messages, each with buttons. Connect Shopify works. Then there are about 8 items scattered through the thread. I scroll back to find which are still open, or I type 'what do you still need?'. That works but I have to remember to ask. Stuck point 1: the list is buried in the conversation.

Upload on phone: tap Upload and choose a file from my phone or Drive. Hard, because I don't keep files on my phone. I forward the request to my staff through the invite button. Stuck point 2: I can't tell which items are Must have versus Helpful without scrolling.

Day 2 reframe: I just type 'actually the real worry is stock running out, how do we grow without it'. This is the easiest of all four since it's all chat. But the earlier messages stay in the thread, so I can't tell what the consultant now thinks the goal is. There's no single place to see the current understanding. Stuck point 3. About 3 min.
Day 3-4: The report arrives as a message in the thread. A long report inside a chat bubble on a phone is awkward to scroll and share. Export to PDF helps.
Abandon risk: medium-low. I won't leave over it, but after 3 days I would lose track of what is outstanding and what changed.
W.quote: Talking is the easiest part. But after two days I don't know what you think my problem is now. I have to scroll up through the whole chat to find out.

walkthrough: Min 0-15: A 5-step guided form on a phone: company, problem category, description, goals, constraints, review. I have to pick a problem category and 'sales drop' doesn't fit neatly. Typing in many small fields on a phone is tiring. I hit the 15-minute limit and the draft is saved, but I may not come back. Stuck points 1 and 2: category choice and form length.

Day 1: Data page with a table of items. A wide table on a phone is a horizontal-scroll problem, so each row's actions (upload, connect, invite) are cramped. Stuck point 3. I invite staff for most items.
Dashboard: tiles for status, 40% data complete, progress %, early charts. I like seeing a percentage. But I don't know what 'analysis progress 30%' means for me.

Day 2 reframe: I realise the real issue is stock. The form was about 'sales drop'. I have to find how to go back and edit the goals and category, and I don't know if changing it restarts the analysis or invalidates the data I already uploaded. Stuck point 4. I'd probably message support. About 10-15 min, with a lot of doubt.
Day 3-4: Report viewable online and as a formal document, good for forwarding. Charts on phone are fine.
Abandon risk: high at the form on day 0, and again at the reframe on day 2. Being forced to commit to a category before I understand my own problem is the problem.
Y.quote: I filled in a form about sales dropping, and two days later I found out that wasn't even the problem. Now I have to dig through the form to change it. I'm not doing that on my phone.

walkthrough: Min 0-2: One page, one text box: 'What's the problem?' I type it. Then 3-5 follow-up questions on the same page. Easy, one thumb.
Min 3-10: Answering questions in a page layout is fine. It's less friendly than chat but quick.

Day 1: The 'Your next step' card tells me exactly what to do and how long it takes (e.g. 'Connect Shopify, 2 min'). I like this most of all four. Then the progress tracker in words. The checklist below is long but I only look at the card. I invite staff for WhatsApp and Odoo data.

Day 2 reframe: 'What we understood' has editable lines. I tap the line 'sales down 20%' and change it to the stock problem. It's direct and visible. But the lines are narrow, and I'm not sure if the other lines and the data checklist update. Stuck point 1: I don't know if the consultant has to re-approve it. There's no chat to just say it. About 5 min.
Day 3: The next-step card changes to 'Waiting on us' with a date. The report moves to the top. One page on a phone means a long scroll, but the structure helps.
Day 4: Read the report on my phone: answer paragraph and steps, then 'How sure are we' per finding. Good enough to act on. Forward to my ops head as PDF.
Abandon risk: low. The only worry is not being able to ask a quick question without a chat.
X.quote: The next-step card is what I need: one thing, how long, who. I changed my problem by editing one line. I just wish I could ask 'why do you need this?' without writing an email.

concepts.X_note: X has no chat for quick questions beyond the shared [Ask a question] on findings.

change_in_favourite: In Z, make the chat a bottom-sheet or tab on phone, so there is no hidden side panel. When I tell it the goal changed, the consultant should reply right away with a plain-language summary of what changes: which earlier data still counts, what new data it needs (stock levels, supplier lead times), and the new date. The page's 'What we understood' should show a visible 'updated just now' line, and the old goal should be crossed out instead of silently gone. Also keep the Must-have items to 3 or fewer on the first screen.
